introduction.text: Casal Rotondo is the largest surviving circular ancient Roman mausoleum on the Appian Way, southeast of Rome, Italy. It is significant as a rare example of Roman funerary architecture and for its later medieval use as a farmhouse and watchtower.

history.description: The mausoleum was constructed around 30 BCE at the sixth mile of the Appian Way.

In the mid‑18th century, Luigi Canina interpreted an epigraphic fragment as evidence that the monument was built by Marcus Aurelius Cotta Maximus Messalinus for his father Marcus Valerius Messalla Corvinus.
A medieval farmhouse was built atop the mausoleum by the Savelli family, serving as a watchtower along the Appian Way.

design.description: The mausoleum is a large circular structure with a diameter of 27 m, originally featuring a conical roof, frieze ornamentation, and seating encircling its base.
